articles.title: MUSE: Revealing Responsiveness Gaps of LLM Tutors on Multiple-Solution Programming Problems
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.36367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a problem admits multiple valid solutions, effective tutoring requires building on a student's strategy while introducing alternatives at appropriate points. However, whether LLM tutors can support this flexibility by appropriately responding to students' diverse solution approaches remains largely unexplored. In this work, we introduce MUSE: Multi-solution Understanding and Simulation Environment, a controlled environment for simulating student-tutor conversations on multiple-solution programming problems. articles.title: Multi-Scale Spatio-Temporal Exploratory Analysis of Urban Vehicle Theft
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.36478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vehicle theft is a persistent urban problem with large economic and social costs. We analyze 521,098 stolen-vehicle reports filed with the Los Angeles Police Department from 2000 to 2022, at scales from hours to decades and from 100 m grid cells to census tracts. Much of the work lies in making the administrative records fit for analysis: we separate thefts from recoveries and traffic reports filed in the same records, repair time fields, validate the geocoding, and harmonize census data across changing tract boundaries. articles.title: Governed Sovereign RAG for Public Administration: Tripartite Epistemic Routing, Facet-Guided Clarification, and Deterministic Numeric Verification in Citizen Services
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.36561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying conversational assistants at government service desks faces a tension between regulatory certainty (zero tolerance for invented fees), data sovereignty prohibiting commercial clouds, and high rates of underspecified or out-of-jurisdiction citizen queries. We present and evaluate a governed, sovereign Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture deployed on the official portal of the State of Tlaxcala, Mexico (tlaxcaladigital.gob.mx), covering 1,143 procedures and a decoupled directory of 924 offices. articles.title: Whether Is Not When: Separating Occurrence from Timing in Polymarket Prices
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.36639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prices formed by Web users on Polymarket, a blockchain-based prediction market, are now cited in the news and in a U.S. Army intelligence bulletin as early warnings of geopolitical events. However, it remains unclear whether these prices can serve as such warnings. This cannot be judged from accuracy, because most markets resolve No and accuracy can remain high even when many of the events that did happen are missed. articles.title: Edhivo: An AI-Native Platform for Scalable Assessment and Instant Feedback in Higher Education
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.36654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling assessment in higher education faces two intertwined bottlenecks: the cognitive burden of authoring assessments and the inability to semantically evaluate open-ended responses, which together create a persistent feedback gap that hinders student learning outcomes. To address these challenges, we present Edhivo, an AI-native pedagogical platform that addresses both bottlenecks through a vertically integrated system for content delivery, assessment, and reporting. articles.title: Conditional Values: The Contingent Foundations of Attitudes toward Artificial Intelligence
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.37197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How do broader values shape whether people judge artificial intelligence (AI) as good or bad for humanity? This article analyzes provisional World Values Survey Wave 8 data from 40,960 respondents in 24 country samples using pooled and national prediction models, outcome-independent respondent profiles, and groups of countries. The analysis reveals a cross-country anchor: general optimism about science and technology is the strongest pooled predictor of favorable AI evaluation and recurs among the leading predictors in every national sample. articles.title: Uneven Use, Similar Trust Generative AI in Denmark and Romania
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.37348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) has spread unevenly across Europe, and it is unclear whether higher use brings higher trust. This paper compares Denmark and Romania, the EU's highest and lowest GenAI users, and asks whether the difference in public and institutional trust between them corresponds to the difference in trust in AI. articles.title: Neighborhood Deprivation Shapes Post-Flood Population Losses in Pune and Bandung
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.37418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disaster research in high-income settings shows that better-resourced communities see population inflows and faster recovery, while disadvantaged communities suffer prolonged population loss. Whether this pattern holds in rapidly urbanizing cities of the Global South remains unclear. articles.title: Extending the W3C Data Privacy Vocabulary to Cover the German Health Data Use Act - Lessons Learned
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.37527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finding, sharing, and reusing data requires common interoperable vocabularies to adequately describe machine-actionable data policies. Semantic Web standards are a proven way to express such information describing data access and reuse. Narrative descriptions get a stable and agreed meaning by formal definitions of terms that have a globally unique identifier. articles.title: People's Views on Smiley Emoji on WeChat Platform, Positive Emotion and Sarcasm
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.35908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Emoji can easily lead to misunderstanding. On WeChat, [Smile] is often used by the elderly to express positive emotions such as joy and praise, but young people often regard [Smile] as sarcasm.
